text.content:
Elected by citizens, bought by corporations.

Kind: City government
Base: City Hall, the Glen
Leadership: Mayor Lucius Rhyne. Arasaka's Accord Liaison, Michiko Arasaka, sits in a non-voting chair
Purpose: Running the Free City, in the interests of whoever sponsors each seat

Night City is run by a Mayor and a City Council of twelve seats, one or two per borough. Every seat has a corporate sponsor, and everyone knows which. Council votes are fixed in the bars of the Glen the night before.

The elected district City Managers of the 2040s were folded into six Borough Offices after the Purge. Where the city doesn't show up, as in Vista del Rey and Pacifica, the gangs run things. Under the Arvin Accord, Arasaka has a non-voting chair at every Council session, and nobody has ever seen it empty.

The Council's Record

  • 1998–2005: After Richard Night's murder the mob moved in; corporate security ended the Mob Wars by hiring more guns than the mob could.
  • 2047: The Council passed both Purge Ordinances, the second in an emergency session thirty-six hours after the lights came back on Static Night. Neither has been repealed.
  • 2052: It auctioned the cleared crater's ring lots; the auction made three councilmen rich.
  • 2070: Its leaked threat-zone reclassification, NCZTA-70, admits which districts it has given up on, and puts Little China and Kabuki on downgrade watch.

Members

  • Mayor Lucius Rhyne, ex-councilman for the Glen, confirmed by acclamation after the Accord.
  • Councilwoman Iris Marchetti represents Downtown. She took Kang Tao money and Militech money in the same week, and survived both.
